item.title: A spoiler-filled The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 interview with Theo actor Tyroe Muhafidin.
item.description:
Warning! Spoilers for The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 Episodes 1-4 follow.
If you’re caught up with The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power, you’ll have watched Season 3, Episode 4 and were probably left reeling by a shock character death that leaves the elves in a spot of bother going into the final stretch.
During the first four episodes of Season 3, we see Theo, played by Tyroe Muhafidin, tempted by Sauron into becoming a Nazgnagôl. Nazgnagôl are men who wear one of Sauron’s Rings of Power, but still retain something of their humanity. That is, they are not fully Nazgûl, or Ringwraiths, as we know of the beings in the Third Age of J. R. R. Tolkien's Middle-earth. They are, at this stage, Ring Servants.
Theo, last seen as a hopeful child of the Southlands and friend of hero elf Arondir, is now older and full of hate after five years of Númenórean oppression. Sauron sees something in him, something special, and offers Theo a gift. In Episode 2, appropriately called The Gift of Men, Sauron performs a dark ritual that lets Theo “meet” his mysterious father, or at least that’s what we think is happening here (with Sauron, you never really know!).
This is a callback to a scene in Season 1 where a young Theo encounters The Hilt, a broken sword-hilt forged during the First Age. It had been left hidden in a barn where Theo discovers it, and we see Theo’s blood drip into the Hilt, somehow feeding its regeneration. Clearly, Theo had some dark power inside him, although it was left unaddressed, sparking many fan theories over recent years.
The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 Photos
In Season 3, Sauron notices the dark mark left on Theo’s arm after his interaction with The Hilt and immediately raises an eyebrow. Who was Theo’s father, really? During the ritual, Sauron uses the power of necromancy to communicate with the dead in the Unseen World. Sauron listens to the words of the dead, and tells Theo his father was named Fäldred, Son of Hammethreg. Theo asks, “Who are you, father?” The response, in Black Speech, is “Gorthmundur.” Sauron tells Theo this was a “Noble House of old, the sworn stewards of Mordor blessed with… certain powers.”
These powers, it seems, were passed down to Theo. “There is a reason you were drawn to that hilt, and it to you,” Sauron continues, before suggesting that Theo might have become ruler of the Southlands had his mother not “hidden the truth.” Theo responds to say his mother told him his father left. Sauron disputes this, before issuing a revelation that sends Theo spiralling: his mother murdered his father over what he had become.
Sauron, ever the opportunist, offers Theo a Ring of Power. He tells him that he has the power within him to become “a conqueror, a sorcerer, a king.” The downcast Theo accepts the gift.
Fast forward to Episode 4, and one of two shock deaths that punctuate this first block of The Rings of Power Season 3. Theo, now in full Nazgnagôl gear and spurred on by Sauron, murders his friend Arondir during the escape from Gundabad. It’s a shocking twist that cements Theo’s descent into darkness, and marks the end of the road for one of the mighty heroes of The Rings of Power.
In the interview below, I ask Tyroe Muhafidin about Theo’s journey in these first four episodes, what it’s like to play a Nazgnagôl, and where the murder of Arondir leaves The Rings of Power. And yes, we get into the question of Theo’s parentage. Was Sauron telling him the truth about his father?
IGN: The first question is an obvious one: how does it feel to be playing a Nazgnagôl?
Tyroe Muhafidin: It was crazy. The costume automatically gives you a sense of such great strength and power. The biggest thing for me was, as soon as I put on those gauntlets there was an automatic transforming moment for me where you could just feel the power through your body. And it's interesting because I went from playing basically a helpless child to some godlike being. So it was a real jump and I had to do a lot of work in terms of my physicality and trying to look powerful and strong, which was something so new to me because I've always been scrawny and helpless. So yeah, it was a challenge, but I think I got there in the end, and I'm super, super grateful that I've got a chance to be something so iconic and to play something so iconic.
IGN: What is your understanding of what Nazgnagôl are, as it was explained to you?
Tyroe Muhafidin: So a Nazgûl directly translates to Ringwraith, whereas Nazgnagôl directly translates to Ring Servant. At this point in time when we've just put the ring on, we're not quite wraiths yet. We are still human men with autonomy over their body and can make their own decisions. We're just a lot stronger now. We've got a lot of power and a lot of dark power.
An important thing to know is at the beginning of this season, the One Ring hasn't yet been made. So these rings are yet to be binded completely to Sauron's will, where we are not now complete, I guess, his minions. We still have autonomy over who we are. That was the fun thing to play in this season, the gradual descent into more and more madness and more and more evil and darkness. But at this point in time, we get to very much still be people, just very strong people, I guess.
IGN: There's a really interesting scene where Sauron reveals Theo's parentage to him. What's your understanding of who Theo's father is? Sauron is suggesting at that moment that Theo has an innate power as a result of his parentage, but it's left ambiguous. And Sauron looks emotional even as he's talking to Theo about this. I almost was thinking he almost looks at him as his own son in some ways. So what's your read on that? What can you tell us about what all that means?
Tyroe Muhafidin: It's revealed that his father was the head of a few dark sorcerers and he sided with the dark side a long time ago, alongside his peers and the other Southlanders who sided with Sauron. And so there's that kind of information that's brought out.
But I think the big thing for Theo is when Sauron says his mother killed him when she found out. And I think that moment for me, and I think for Theo as a whole, it kind of sends a spin in the works of, what is Sauron really doing here and what is he trying to accomplish? Is he just trying to say words to make Theo happy, trying to build this broken boy up? Because he can see something for sure. And I don't think Theo really realizes. But I think there was always a dark side to Theo and maybe it was inherited, but that relationship to the Hilt was always something that stuck with him.
And I think maybe when he got a taste of that darkness in the Hilt, maybe it was the first time he kind of felt the presence of his father, and maybe that's why it was so addictive, that feeling to him. So I think this season we find out a little bit more of where he comes from.
But I think the biggest thing is, how much of it is the truth? What is Sauron saying that is manipulation and deceit and what is the truth? Which I think is kind of the fun dynamic of those scenes, is you feel like you're finding out a lot, but are you really?
IGN: There is a big moment in Episode 4 where Theo kills Arondir, a character who's been in the series from the beginning. When you first found out you'd be doing that, what was your reaction?
Tyroe Muhafidin: It was interesting. I was excited because I was like, "Oh, this is some juicy stuff to get into." But I think the moment I got the script, I found out and I was really excited because it was going to be some really cool stuff. When I read it all, it all became very real for me. And it was like, "Wow, this is a big task. This is super daunting." And there were months of intense anxiety coming up to this moment. But yeah, I guess I was just super excited, but anxious at the same time. And I feel like I knew at some point something big like this was going to happen. So I think it was just a matter of being prepared for it and trying to service Ismail [Cruz Córdova, who plays Arondir] as well, the best I possibly could.
IGN: What do you think the character death means for the show at that point and the story it's telling, but also for Theo? Do you see it as this is a moment that we see a tipping point in him that the audience is like, "Okay, yes, he has really gone too far."
Tyroe Muhafidin: In terms of the show, it's a moment of no-one is safe and there's no mercy from the dark side. And this war is very much real. The most talented and bravest of your warriors will go down. And that's kind of, I think, setting the premise for the rest of the war that's going to go on.
I think for Theo specifically, it definitely was that tipping point where his decision is made and his destiny is decided. And I think he realizes this afterwards as well, and whether he agrees with that decision he's made or not, he's made that decision.
The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 episodes 1-4 are out now on Prime Video. Check back with IGN after Episodes 5 and 6 are released this week for more.

item.title: James Gunn has shut down rumors that the new DC overseers at Skydance have meddled with his cut of Man of Tomorrow following his shocking DC Studios exit.
item.description:
James Gunn has shut down rumors that the new DC overseers at Skydance have meddled with his cut of Man of Tomorrow following his shocking DC Studios exit.
The internet has filled with gossip in the wake of Gunn and Peter Safran's departure as co-chairmen of the comic book entertainment wing earlier this week. As an ocean of rumors rises, some of the more worrying claims have seen some suggest Skydance has already taken control of the Superman director's sequel, which could result in major characters like Supergirl and Blue Beetle being cut entirely.
These are just some of the accusations that Gunn sought to dispel in a Threads post tonight. In what is essentially his first public statement since leaving DC Studios, the filmmaker took aim at the gossip that has DCU fans concerned. Not only have "sweeping changes" to Man of Tomorrow not been made, but apparently, no one at Skydance has even seen his movie yet.
"There are a lot of untrue rumors going around, but one of them is that Skydance has seen Man of Tomorrow and that all sorts of sweeping changes are being made," he said. "No one from Skydance has even seen the movie - the only people that have are Peter Safran and a very small trusted group of friends and family. So any stories around this narrative are false."
It's a response that will not answer every question comic book movie enjoyers have about the future of the DCU, but it does clear the air about much of the more damning chatter online. Gunn's comments mean that any talk of Skydance being unhappy with the current cut of Man of Tomorrow is false. It also sounds like, at least for now, Supergirl and Blue Beetle, who had been previously reported to return, are safe.
With so much time left before David Corenswet's Clark Kent returns to theaters in July, though, it's hard to say how the Skydance takeover may impact its release. It's best to wait until Gunn or Skydance has more to share before setting any firm expectations in place for now.
All of that said, it's not too hard to see why fans of the DCU have felt uneasy in the last few days. Gunn and Safran have orchestrated the DCU to tell a varied collection of superpowered stories for four years, with its overarching plan for the years ahead only just starting to come into view. Pulling them from the driver's seat means the future is more unknown than ever before, especially considering Skydance was quick to find a replacement in Marvel alum Jeremy Latcham.
Will Man of Tomorrow be altered against Gunn's will? Will Skydance reboot the DC movie universe and scrap future plans for the DCU? How will any of this affect future entries in Robert Pattinson's The Batman saga? It's all too soon to tell, but that won't stop the rumor mill from pushing ahead.
What we do know is what Gunn shared with fans in the immediate aftermath of his exit. In a letter posted to social media, he promised that the characters he and Safran helped set up "will live on." He also confirmed that the duo was recently "engaged on another DC project" that he is writing. What that project is remains a mystery.
Do you want to see Skydance reboot the DCU?

item.title: Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson, executive producers for Blade Runner 2099 and co-CEOs of Alcon Entertainment, have confirmed that they are in discussions to create a AAA video game based on the iconic cyberpunk franchise.
item.description:
Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson, executive producers for Blade Runner 2099 and co-CEOs of Alcon Entertainment, the owner of the Blade Runner franchise, have confirmed that they are in discussions to create a AAA video game based on the iconic cyberpunk IP.
I got the chance to chat with Kosove and Johnson ahead of Blade Runner 2099’s release on Prime Video later this month. During our conversation, I brought up the wildly successful Cyberpunk 2077, wondering why Blade Runner hasn’t had a similar AAA game made after it and if any conversations have been had about finally giving this IP a major modern video game release.
“Yes,” Kosove confirmed, and emphasized the phrase “AAA,” making it clear that Alcon has a grand vision for Blade Runner’s future in the gaming space. Of course, he couldn’t tell me much more, but impressed upon the importance of allowing players to “interact” with the world of Blade Runner in this hypothetical game.
Blade Runner 2099 Images
This is big news for fans of Blade Runner and the cyberpunk genre, in general. While Blade Runner has enjoyed its status as a cult-classic and cornerstone of modern science fiction, it hasn’t exactly been blessed in the game department.
Based on IGN’s own list of Blade Runner games, the franchise has four licensed titles. The first, published in 1985 by CRL Group PLC for the Commodore 64, is an absolute dinosaur of a game that wasn’t well-received even at the time of its release. In the game, players hunt down replicants (here, replidroids) for bounty money. Due to the cost of movie rights at the time, this game was said to merely be “inspired” by the "Vangelis soundtrack" of Ridley Scott’s 1982 film and not a direct adaptation.
The next Blade Runner game, which was released in 1997, enjoyed far more critical acclaim and is still considered a classic to this day. Developed by Westwood Studios and published by Virgin Interactive, this point-and-click adventure title was one of the very first titles to use 3D character models and real-time environments. A remake was released in 2022.
Another game, titled Blade Runner 2033: Labyrinth, was announced in 2023 and developed by Annapurna Interactive. Unfortunately, the project is now largely considered to be canceled, having been delisted from Steam and removed from Annapurna’s website. (Blade Runner 2049: Replicant Pursuit was released in 2017. It was a short, tie-in VR experience meant to promote the second film, but not a full, official game.)
Given that it’s been nearly 30 years since Blade Runner fans have had a fresh, critically acclaimed video game adaptation, this latest news is extremely exciting and opens up an entire world of possibilities. And considering Kosove’s focus on player interactivity and AAA quality, it sounds like Alcon has a clear vision for what it wants this game to be — and I can’t wait to see what they come up with.
Blade Runner 2099 releases on Prime Video on November 25.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: Sony has confirmed Marvel's Spider-Man 2, Arc Raiders, and four more games are receiving QSSR support on base PS5s.
item.description:
Sony has confirmed Marvel's Spider-Man 2, Arc Raiders, and four more games are receiving QSSR support on base PS5s.
The list of six newcomers joining the small-but-growing group of supported games was unveiled in a PlayStation.Blog post. In addition to confirmation that incoming updates will add QSSR (Quick Spectral Super Resolution), the post included testimonials from each of the studios' developers, who shared how the tech will impact visuals.
When Sony pulled back the curtain on QSSR in October, it came with confirmation that it had already been implemented in Marvel's Wolverine and Ghost of Yōtei. Now, we know that Insomniac's Marvel's Spider-Man 2, Remedy Entertainment's Control Resonant, Embark Studios' Arc Raiders and The Finals, Hello Games' No Man's Sky, and Expression Games' Hell Let Loose: Vietnam will soon take advantage of the AI upscaling tech.
In the case of Marvel's Spider-Man 2, QSSR is available as part of a new update that's out now.
"Having seen great results integrating QSSR in Marvel’s Wolverine, our team decided to bring it to Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 as well, in an update that’s live now!" Insomniac head of technology Mike Fitzgerald said. "We’re excited for players to swing back into our 2023 title and see QSSR’s exciting image stability and sharpness benefits in both Fidelity and Performance modes."
Remedy said QSSR will bring noticeable improvements in image stability and fine detail when it launches in a new update in December. Hello Games founder Sean Murray, meanwhile, promised that players can look forward to No Man's Sky looking "sharper, cleaner, and more beautiful" at the "best possible framerate" in the next few weeks. When exactly The Finals, Arc Raiders, and Hell Let Loose: Vietnam will receive their updates has yet to be announced.
PS5 Digital Console 30th Anniversary Limited Edition
"With the new QSSR coming soon to ARC Raiders and The Finals, we can deliver increased sharpness, better environmental clarity, and overall visual improvements to even more PlayStation players," Embark said. "We are very happy to see Sony’s continued investment in PlayStation technology translate into meaningful improvements for all players, bringing more immersive experiences across the PlayStation ecosystem."
Sony then teased that developers interested in using QSSR are "just getting started." More PS5 games are set to receive similar updates in the coming months, though which titles will join the list remains to be seen.
Do you care about AI performance in your gaming PC if it's not used for upscaling?

item.title: Marvel actor Paul Bettany has said Kevin Feige didn't want Elizabeth Olsen's Wanda Maximoff to be in VisionQuest because he was worried she might "distract" from the show's core.
item.description:
Marvel actor Paul Bettany has said Kevin Feige didn't want Elizabeth Olsen's Wanda Maximoff to be in VisionQuest because he was worried she might "distract" from the show's core.
The Marvel Cinematic Universe star recalled the conversation he had with the Marvel Studios bigwig when speaking with The Playlist. MCU followers spent the months leading up to the new Disney+ offshoot speculating about how it may serve as a vehicle for an unlikely resurrection.
Those who have kept up with the nearly 20-year-old cinematic universe will remember that Wanda met her end in the closing moments of 2022's Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness. She's yet to be seen since, and although discussions about seeing her share a screen with Vision were had, Bettany said it was an idea Feige was never too fond of.
VisionQuest Images
"There were questions about it, whether that should happen, whether it opened up too much for the MCU, whether they wanted to do it later," he remembered. "I don't know. But I remember having this conversation with [Kevin], and he said, 'You and Terry have done such a great job at making me care about Vision. I really don’t think you should distract from that by giving the audience that at the end of the [show].
"It will just fundamentally all become about WandaVision again, and this should and can stand on its own.' And I think he was right."
The main events of VisionQuest came and went without any signs that Olsen had recorded new footage to fit directly within VisionQuest, leaving the MCU without a proper family reunion. It was a disappointing moment for those who had spent months speculating she would reappear ahead of Avengers: Doomsday as theories were finally put to rest.
Every WandaVision Episode Review
Warning! Spoilers for VisionQuest's finale credits scenes follow.
If you've finished VisionQuest, you'll know that disappointment didn't last long. Just as the final credits for the finale episode came to an end, viewers were taken back to Wanda's resting place on the snowy cliffs of Mount Wundagore. There, a cloaked figure that looks and sounds a lot like Robert Downey Jr.'s Victor von Doom reaches out to her, saying, "Scarlet Witch, awaken. Your power will be mine." Then, her eyes open.
Yes, Olsen and Wanda Maximoff are coming back, with the return set up alongside VisionQuest's finale, despite Feige's wishes. To be fair, the reveal mostly seemed to consist of reused footage from her appearance in the Doctor Strange sequel. The scene is also just about as far removed from VisionQuest itself as it can be. So, while Feige may have wanted to avoid Wanda distracting from the partial family reunion we got in VisionQuest, her inclusion at least managed to arrive long after the main story wrapped up.
We'll hopefully know more about Wanda's future – and hopefully whether or not she'll reunite with Vision, Billy, and Tommy – when Avengers: Doomsday premieres next month, December 18. Until then, you can check out what IGN thought of VisionQuest's finale in our 7/10 review.
"The last-minute addition of a new villain derails the finale of VisionQuest somewhat," we said, "but the series still succeeds where Vision and Ultron are concerned."

item.title: Ubisoft has reportedly given a new entry in the Rainbow Six: Vegas series the green light and a codename.
item.description:
Ubisoft has reportedly given a new entry in the Rainbow Six: Vegas series the green light and a codename.
Details on a long-awaited (and unexpected) return to a fan-favorite corner of the Rainbow Six universe come from an Insider Gaming report. The publisher is said to have given its Ubisoft Montreal team the go-ahead to begin work on a new Vegas installment, with two other projects reportedly also in the works there.
Rainbow Six: Vegas started with the release of the original game in 2006 before it returned for a sequel in 2008. Whether the new game will be called Rainbow Six: Vegas 3 or something else is unclear, though the site's sources say it's expected to be more like the former rather than something like a remake. It also stated that it's being worked on with the apt codename, "Spades."
That's just one of the three games the Montreal studio is reportedly working on. The report wasn't able to confirm much about the remaining projects but said one source suggested at least one other game is planned to take place in the Rainbow Six universe in some capacity.
The Rainbow Six franchise as a whole existed long before popular entries like Rainbow Six Siege or even the Vegas series. Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six traces all the way back to the late '90s but has splintered into a wide variety of gameplay experiences and offerings. Siege is no doubt the most well-known iteration today thanks to how Ubisoft has supported its tactical gameplay since its 2015 launch, but the most recent entry actually arrived in 2022 with Rainbow Six Extraction.
Despite nearly 20 years passing since the last Vegas game, it's remained a beloved corner of the universe for many. IGN gave the original game a 7.6/10 when it launched for PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360. We then gave the sequel's limited edition release an 8.4/10.
Rainbow Six Tactics - First Screenshots
Ubisoft seems to be still in the early stages of its unannounced Rainbow Six: Vegas continuation, so don't expect to see it launch for at least a few more years. While that may mean we'll have passed the 20-year mark since the last game, we hopefully won't have to wait quite as long to learn more about it. Until then, it's best to keep expectations low while the publisher keeps its cards close to its chest.
Meanwhile, we do know about a few other projects Ubisoft has up its sleeve. Rainbow Six Tactics, for example, was announced in August and will launch sometime next year. A Splinter Cell remake is also in the works, even if it's been a while since we heard from it.
Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

item.title: Purported details of Robert Pattinson’s screen test deal to audition for James Bond 26 have come to light, and they reveal that he’s being treated differently than the four other actors in contention.
item.description:
Purported details of Robert Pattinson’s screen test deal to audition for James Bond 26 have come to light, and they reveal that he’s being treated differently than the four other actors in contention.
According to Puck’s Matthew Belloni, as part of auditioning for the role of 007, the five actors on the shortlist – Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor, Nicholas Hoult and Pattinson – all had to sign contracts agreeing to be in Bond 26 plus options for subsequent sequels. That’s all standard procedure on Bond films, including when Daniel Craig auditioned for Casino Royale.
At 40, Pattinson is not just the oldest of the actors vying for 007 but also the biggest star (and, thus, the most expensive choice).
Puck claims Pattinson and Hoult screen-tested after the other three actors did, which might suggest Amazon MGM, producers David Heyman and Amy Pascal, and director Denis Villeneuve weren’t entirely happy with the tests from the lesser known actors.
While past James Bond actors have largely been unknown (Roger Moore and Pierce Brosnan were TV stars), the speculation is that the 60+ year-old franchise could use a boost from a known actor who appeals to younger audiences and would thus minimize commercial risks for the studio.
“Pattinson’s test deal was so difficult to close, per two sources familiar with the process, that some involved were left wondering why the filmmakers would bother if they didn’t really [their emphasis] want him,” Belloni writes.
Who should play 007 in Denis Villeneuve's James Bond?

item.title: The Game Awards is coming to Roblox for the first time this December, complete with live voting, virtual merchandise, and the opportunity to experience the whole thing alongside other players.
item.description:
The Game Awards is coming to Roblox for the first time this December, giving fans another way to watch Geoff Keighley's annual gaming shindig, complete with live voting, virtual merchandise, and the opportunity to experience the whole thing alongside other players.
The Game Awards 2026 will stream live on Roblox starting Thursday, December 10, marking the first time an external awards show has been livestreamed on the platform. The broadcast will take place in The Block, Roblox's virtual event venue, while the actual ceremony takes place at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. There's a catch, though. Only Roblox users aged 18 and older will be able to attend the virtual watch party.
Those who are old and wizened enough to take part will be able to watch the entire broadcast, including the usual assortment of world premieres, new game announcements, awards, and musical performances. Fans will also be able to vote, interact with other viewers, and claim virtual merchandise, although exactly what that merchandise will look like remains to be seen. Official category voting will also be available ahead of the ceremony, with further details about the Roblox experience expected closer to the event.
On December 10th, #TheGameAwards makes history as the show will stream live in @Roblox for the first time. Fans 18+ will be able to watch, vote and interact LIVE alongside gaming's biggest night.More details coming soon. https://t.co/ouVtxXt7yV
The Block is no stranger to hosting major events. The virtual venue has previously been home to the Roblox Innovation Awards, alongside music experiences featuring artists including Billie Eilish, The Rolling Stones, and (K-pop fan hyperventilating) Stray Kids.
The Game Awards 2026 takes place December 10, with Geoff Keighley once again at the helm. There's no word yet on exactly how the virtual merchandise or interactive elements will work, but more details are promised in the coming weeks. It will also be available to stream through Disney+.
At the very least, watching The Game Awards in Roblox should make for an interesting alternative to sitting through several hours of announcements while arguing about Game of the Year in a group chat. Now you can do it surrounded by avatars instead.
Rachel Weber is the Head of Editorial Development at IGN and an elder millennial. She's been a professional nerd since 2006 when she got her start on Official PlayStation Magazine in the UK, and has since worked for GamesIndustry.Biz, Rolling Stone and GamesRadar. She loves horror, horror movies, horror games, Red Dead Redemption 2, and her Love and Deepspace boyfriends.

item.title: A Star Wars auction has just broken records, as Darth Vader's prop lightsaber from the original trilogy sells for almost $5 million.
item.description:
A prop lightsaber wielded by Darth Vader in the original Star Wars trilogy has just sold at auction for almost $5 million.
This is the most amount of money a Star Wars prop has ever sold for, and it’s easy to see why. The lightsaber was featured in The Empire Strikes Back — largely seen as the best of the bunch — and Return of the Jedi, making it at least 46 years old.
As reported by The Guardian, the sale was done through Heritage Auctions, and sold for $4.875 million. The eye-watering figure beat the previous overall record of $3,875,000, which Heritage achieved with Tom Jung’s original half-sheet key poster painting for Star Wars: Episode IV – A New Hope. It also eclipsed the previous record for a screen-used Star Wars prop: Heritage’s $3,750,000 sale of Luke Skywalker’s lightsaber and severed hand effects rig on July 15, 2026.
"Vader’s lightsaber is an artifact from the very heart of the saga, and its result led a historic auction," Joe Maddalena, Heritage’s Executive Vice President, said.
The item description gives us some more details on the prop itself. For instance, this is the version that was used when the lightsabers were “ignited," so there are “mounting bolts” that would have been used to attach a wooden blade, later edited to look like a lightsaber. Because of this, we know it would have been used by both David Prowse (the guy usually in the Darth Vader suit) and Bob Anderson, who handled fight scenes and stunts.
In other words, yes, this is the lightsaber that was on-screen during the fight on Bespin between Vader and Luke.
How Much Every Star Wars Movie Made Opening Weekend
Other items up for grabs during the auction included prop blasters, figurines, and script drafts. However, none of them came even close to amassing the same amount of interest as the lightsabers used in the most iconic scene from the entire franchise. It’s hard to see what could top this now.
Nostalgia for the original Star Wars trilogy is in full effect, with Disney announcing plans for the first movie and the franchise's 50th anniversary this week. A fresh documentary detailing the making of A New Hope, George Lucas' original Star Wars film, will appear on Disney+ on May 4th next year. The Hero Awakens includes rare archival footage from A New Hope's production, helmed by Academy Award-nominated filmmaker R.J. Cutler.
The documentary follows the theatrical re-release of Star Wars on February 19. This will be the rarely-seen original 1977 version of the movie.
Which Star Wars project are you most excited for?

item.title: Wizards of the Coast and Netflix have revealed their long-in-development Magic: The Gathering series is called Planeswalker, and it's coming sometime in 2027.
item.description:
There's been a Magic: The Gathering animated series cooking in the background since 2019, and now at MagicCon Atlanta, Wizards of the Coast has revealed that it's called Planeswalker, and it's coming sometime in 2027.
Rather than being some epic live-action fantasy show like Game of Thrones, Netflix is taking the same approach it did with Castlevania and making Planeswalker an animated series. But making a show in a universe as expansive as Magic: The Gathering is challenging, due to the nearly infinite worlds it encompasses. It sounds like the show isn't shying away from that.
The show will be centered on Planeswalker Chandra Nalaar. According to a synopsis shared with IGN, she's "a volatile pyromancer hunted for her gifts, and haunted by her past. Confronted by an insidious force, Chandra and some of the most legendary Planeswalkers must harness their extraordinary abilities, navigate treacherous alliances, and battle their own inner demons to prevent a cataclysmic war that threatens to consume their very existence. As the line between victory and annihilation grows thinner, a single spark determines the fate of thousands of worlds."
Every great story begins with a spark. Here’s your first look at PLANESWALKER, a new animated series based on Magic: The Gathering. Coming to Netflix in 2027. https://t.co/7tQNJaFPrU
Chandra was also the character that appeared in the first teaser for the show years ago, so it looks like this is still the same thing. However, when Netflix first announced that it'd be working on a Magic: The Gathering series back in 2019, it had Avengers: Endgame directors Joe and Anthony Russo running the show. The Russo Brothers left back in 2021, and in the five years since then, ownership of the show has passed to Terry Matalas, who will be running it alongside Cindy Appel.
Matalas previously served as the showrunner for VisionQuest, which just ended and was well received. In the IGN review, we gave the premiere a 7, and reviewer Jesse Schedeen said, "VisionQuest may struggle a bit to reestablish the titular hero in this post-WandaVision MCU, but at least the series has James Spader’s Ultron to fall back upon."
MagicCon Atlanta Preview Panel – Screenshots
Magic: The Gathering has a ton of lore to build a show off of, and it's going to be interesting to see how it handles a multiverse that'd put Marvel to shame. At least we won't have to wait too long before it debuts in 2027. Let's just hope Netflix doesn't wait until November to put it out.
Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

item.title: The next map confirmed for Crazy Taxi: World Tour is India, boasting three different zones that celebrate the country’s many cultures and hallmarks — and yes, Bollywood films make an appearance.
item.description:
The next map confirmed for Crazy Taxi: World Tour is India, boasting three different zones that celebrate the country’s many cultures and hallmarks — and yes, Bollywood films make an appearance.
Crazy Taxi: World Tour will boast five international maps: the US West Coast, Germany, Japan, Brazil, and finally, India. The India map will feature three distinct zones, labeled City, Countryside, and Industrial.
The City zone is all hustle and bustle, with vibrant marketplaces, nightlife, and architecture. The Country zone is where you can find ancient temples and zoom through the natural landscape, while the Industrial zone takes players on a tour of its trade and commerce hubs, as well as a look at one of the world’s oldest trains.
The game’s official trailer for the India map even teases that players might find themselves on the “set of a Bollywood film,” showing a passenger holding a camera who appears to be a movie director.
This is the latest news to come from this highly-anticipated installment in Sega’s beloved arcade racing game after a closed beta test gave fans a hint at what its multiplayer mode might look like. A signup website for the test says players could participate in two different modes: Pickup Race and Cops ‘N’ Cabbies.
In the Pickup Race mode, up to 6 players compete to drop off as many passengers as possible within a specific time limit and earn as much cash as they can. In Cops ‘N’ Cabbies, two teams of players face off against each other, with one being cabbies and the other being cops hot on their trail.
In addition to multiplayer, the game also has a story mode that follows its main character, Axel, as he chases a gang of international car thieves across the globe to recover his stolen ride, bussing passengers across each country along the way.
We got the chance to preview Crazy Taxi: World Tour back in August. IGN’s Scott White praised the game for its “simple-yet-exciting sort of fun that arcade games excel at, that makes you want to just keep playing,” calling it an “almost refreshingly uncomplicated palette cleanser free of skill trees, crafting systems, and the other chaff that seems to be in every game you play nowadays.”
Crazy Taxi: World Tour launches in early 2027 on Xbox X|S, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and PC.

item.title: Marvel has confirmed the lineup of heroes that Anthony Mackie's Captain America will lead into battle when Avengers: Doomsday premieres next month.
item.description:
Marvel has confirmed the lineup of heroes that Anthony Mackie's Captain America will lead into battle when Avengers: Doomsday premieres next month.
Which portion of the big team-up movie's ensemble cast will fall specifically into the Avengers camp was confirmed by Empire. During an interview with some of the movie's cast and crew, the minds behind the Marvel Cinematic Universe talked about what each hero is bringing into the fight and which camp they have ultimately fallen into.
With so many different teams from across the MCU multiverse to keep track of, you may have been a bit confused about who was fighting who and which superpowered being was on whose side. For Mackie, returning as Captain America means leading a new team, and that team now officially encompasses him, Falcon (Danny Ramirez), Ant-Man (Paul Rudd), Thor (Chris Hemsworth), and Shang-Chi (Simu Liu).
Hot Toys' Avengers: Doomsday Figures - Image Gallery
The full team includes faces new and old as Earth's Mightiest Heroes band together to fight off Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom. It'll be far from Mackie's first rodeo as Sam Wilson, but donning the Captain America mantle represents a completely new moment not only for himself but for the characters he's leading. He opened up about the role change during the interview.
"In Endgame, Steve gave him the shield and says, 'You need to be the leader of the Avengers,'" he said. "Now you get to see more of him leading the charge with everyone into battle."
Although we know little about what exactly Doctor Doom's master plan entails, we do know that the primary Avengers team will have some help. Classic X-Men characters and the recently established Fantastic Four will be there to help, too, as will the motley crew of half-heroes known as the New Avengers. The group will almost certainly clash with the classic Avengers lineup, with wild cards like Steve Rogers (Chris Evans) sure to throw a wrench into things, too.
Ranking Phase Five of the MCU
There's… a lot going on in the MCU, but Avengers: Doomsday will give everyone a chance to get their act together. Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige also explained what kind of team viewers can expect.
"We're coming out of years of seemingly no organized Avengers team, and that's exactly when they face these incursions," he said, referencing a post-credits scene from the recently released Avengers: Endgame Encore. "That’s always fun, to put your heroes on the back foot."
How are you feeling about the future of Marvel post Avengers: Doomsday?

item.title: A collector has discovered and authenticated what's believed to be the only surviving, playable copy of PokéPark Fishing Rally, a temporary fishing minigame that was only available to play via wireless download at PokéPark in Japan in 2005.
item.description:
From May to September 2005, guests at PokéPark — a theme park in Nagoya, Japan centered on Nintendo’s world-famous monster-catching game franchise —could take part in an especially unique, limited-time gaming experience available only for attendees.
This experience was centered around a game called PokéPark Fishing Rally, a fishing minigame that staff wirelessly transferred to guests’ DS handheld consoles via Download Play stations set inside the Park. The game itself was only available on players’ consoles for a 12-hour period after being downloaded, and would erase itself if the DS was powered off. It featured a slew of catchable Water-Type Pokémon, as well as multiple fishing locations and even cameos from non-catchable Pokémon.
Players would compete with other attendees to fish out Pokémon in special events, contests, and organized activities. Surviving photos taken at the Park show that leaderboards were displayed to help competitors keep track of their progress. It’s been twenty years since then, and Nintendo’s unique PokéPark Fishing Rally game had all but faded from the public consciousness… until now.
The Best Pokémon Spin-off Games
In July 2026, a player posted an eBay listing for a physical development cartridge of PokéPark Fishing Rally that contained a leaderboard of past attendees’ scores. At first, it was believed to be the only surviving cartridge for this extremely specific title — but now, another collector has come forward with a playable copy of the full game.
Daniel Quadri, an avid collector and Pokémon enthusiast, approached IGN with evidence showing that he is in possession of a functioning PokéPark Fishing Rally cartridge, which is capable of transmitting the game to other DS consoles through Download Play.
To prove that his find was legit and that it actually worked, he sent us exclusive photos and videos showing him running the game on a DS handheld, as well as sending it to other DS consoles that were able to play it. In fact, his discovery was so monumental that he sent it to PSA for authentication, which catalogued and encapsulated the cartridge for posterity.
"I have come across things considered lost media several times in my career. However, this is the first time I have encountered it from a franchise as societally and personally important as Pokémon is. It was an honor and a privilege to experience this game first-hand,” Head of PSA Video Games, Claire Shelton, told IGN in an exclusive statement.
“We are always proud to play a role in documenting, authenticating, and encapsulating unique pieces of video game history such as this. Our involvement allows the item to continue existing and potentially transact with full confidence to any collector, assuring them that this unique piece is assuredly one of the only ways to interact with this formerly lost media piece of Pokémon history."
“PokéPark had some incredible attractions in 2005, and PokéPark: Tsuri Taikai DS, also known as PokéPark Fishing Rally DS, made the experience even more immersive. Fans could catch Pokémon in 3D on their Nintendo DS as they explored the park and entered contests for a chance to win prizes. Imagine being one of those kids and finding out years later that the game you played that day had become a piece of lost Pokémon media,” Quadri said in a separate statement to IGN.
PokéPark Fishing Rally Game & Merchandise
“Pokémon started with video games and grew into a world of manga, trading cards and anime. That’s why preserving a game like this means so much to me. After years of fans wondering if it would ever be playable again, it felt surreal to turn on my DS and spend a quiet moment fishing, then feel that rush when I reeled in a Gyarados. For a moment, I got to feel what it must have been like to play it at PokéPark in 2005.
“What fascinates me is that visitors at PokéPark could download the game wirelessly to their own Nintendo DS back in 2005. With this cartridge in my DS, I can recreate that experience today. I can send the full game directly to someone else’s DS through Download Play, without needing a download station.”
Due to the game’s purposefully temporary nature, and the fact that it was never publicly released or officially distributed, it was generally assumed that nobody would ever get to play PokéPark Fishing Rally again. Quadri did not share exactly how he came into possession of this game, but his discovery is extremely exciting, regardless — and it isn’t the only piece of PokéPark memorabilia he’s collected.
Quadri also shared images and videos of various magazines, brochures, and even merchandise from the PokéPark experience, one of which advertises a Summer Vacation Challenge. In the challenge, the first 200 people to catch a specific ‘target Pokémon’ would earn a special Nintendo DS scratch guard as a prize. A decorative fan was also on offer with advertising for the activity.
If you're so inclined, you can read one woman's firsthand account of her time at PokéPark on her blog, where she recounts her boyfriend's one-in-a-million Shiny Magikarp catch. She even included a photo to commemorate the moment, which, as Quadri puts it, must have felt like "winning the lottery." As most shiny hunters will know, repeatedly restarting your device is a common tactic to increase your chances at snagging a shiny 'mon; given that this game would literally delete itself if that happened, the odds of coming across such a find in such a short amount of time is nothing short of a miracle, and a good example of how special PokéPark was.
This is the latest rare Nintendo find to make headlines after a collector came upon a box of 97 sealed copies of an unreleased version of Super Mario Bros. Duck Hunt earlier this year.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: Just a couple days after Blizzard changed the way gold was earned in max-level quests WoW Forever, the company has implemented a weekly quest with loot-box-style gold reward. And players don't love it.
item.description:
Just a couple days after Blizzard changed the way gold was earned in max-level quests WoW Forever, the company has implemented a weekly quest with loot-box-style gold reward. And players don't love it.
Max level players have found a quest in Booty Bay called 'In Demand - Ancient Elven Curiosities,' which is offered each week, according to Wowhead. There is potential that the quest will rotate to different high level dungeons, but so far, for the two weeks Forever has been out, it's pointed players at Dire Maul, where they have to collect three items. The quest rewards a little bag that can drop one of four items at random that are worth either 10g, 20g, 40g, or 100g.
But while this is a way to get gold in a game where money is scarce, it is rubbing a lot of players in the community the wrong way. For a lot of people, it reminds them of retail WoW, which is built on top of piles and piles of weekly quests to pump additional gold into the economy.
World of Warcraft: Forever Screenshots
WoW YouTuber Bellular posted the Wowhead link on X / Twitter, captioned simply by "uh what," and followed that up with some criticisms of the new weekly quest. He said: "Retail slop, kill! The way to generate gold is crafting, gathering, selling items. Want to do UBI? Make it sneaky via those means. Don’t show the hand of the designer so clearly." Bellular then tagged Blizzard associate production director Clayton Stone and added: "(pardon the spicy language - some genuine feedback) Let the player earn organically through game systems, not by making content a hoop to jump through."
But it's not just Bellular who's upset at the weekly quest. It's a similar sentiment over on Reddit, where ThatOldGuy7863 simply said: "dear god not weeklys." Meanwhile, drtakhs added: "F**k weeklies and dailies. I’ve been pretty happy with all the decision so far and the thought process behind them was reasonable. Now, what is this? Who wants this? No dailies, no weeklies and no FOMO bulls**t are among the most important things that make classic feel… well like classic…"
However, there may be an explanation for Blizzard's move here. EvadableMoxie suggested a repeatable quest for 100 gold "is aggressively anti-bot."
"It reduces the biggest benefit that bots have, the ability to run 24/7 by frontloading gold rewards," the continued. "This of course does not make bots useless but it reduces their advantage while letting players focus on other things than grinding out gold."
Blizzard has long struggled with bots messing with the economy in every version of World of Warcraft. In the beta, the company had to come down hard on people who were buying and selling gold, which is a direct consequence of botting. Simply put, it's not hard to program a bot to crawl zones for you and gather mining, herbalism or other materials to sell en masse on the auction house. A weekly quest that rewards gold could help players that don't have the time to compete with bots dumping industrial amounts of crafting materials keep up.
But players aren't mad that Blizzard is adding a way to earn gold. Rather, it's the addition of a weekly quest, that encourages players to log on every single week for fear of missing out on an injection of gold. This sort of repeatable quest also wasn't in the original game, with most types of daily and weekly quests not being added until The Burning Crusade.
This is just the latest change as Blizzard tries to nail down the identity of WoW Forever. While there are some parts of the original game that the company has stood firm on, like group tagging, there is an ever growing list of gameplay systems that Blizzard is actively tweaking in Forever, like Dungeon Experience and now, gold rewards.
World of Warcraft Forever or Retail?

item.title: Sony has revealed that God of War Sons of Sparta is coming to PS4 next week, and it's bringing two new modes with it.
item.description:
Sony has revealed that God of War Sons of Sparta is coming to PS4 next week, and it's bringing two new modes with it.
The unexpected update for this year's action platformer prequel was announced in a PlayStation.Blog post today. In it, Sony confirmed plans to bring Kratos' earliest adventure to the last-gen console starting midnight local time November 16.
It's more than a surprise bonus platform, too, as developer Mega Cat Studios has promised two new modes that will be available on both PS4 and PS5: Hermes Mode and Erebus Mode. The former is described as a "race against the clock" that features speedrunning tools like a split-based timer and a persistent scoreboard. The latter is a one-hit-kill mode that affects both Kratos and his enemies.
God Of War Sons of Sparta Screenshots
Sony and Mega Cat tell God of War Sons of Sparta players that they'll be able to select their mode when starting a new game and selecting a save slot. Game modes can't be changed once selected. Hermes Mode, specifically, is activated only after beating the game once through and after players input the following code: Up, Up, Down, Down, Left, Right, Left, Right, L1, R1, Touchpad. It's unclear if unlocking Erebus Mode has a similar old-school cheat code-esque requirement.
God of War Sons of Sparta takes one of PlayStation's most popular exclusive franchises and scales it down to let players control Kratos at a much, much earlier point in his life in ancient Greece. Shadow-dropped back in February of this year as an experimental chapter of the story for PS5, its story returns to an era fans have longed for with original Kratos actor Terrence 'T.C. Carson back in the booth.
"Every legend has a beginning – before he was a God, before he was a father, Kratos was a young Spartan!" an official story description said. "Experience an untold chapter in Kratos’ journey set during the harsh years of Spartan training alongside his brother Deimos. Through endless trials, their minds, bodies, and hearts have been molded to become Spartan soldiers for whom duty and honor mean everything. After a fellow cadet goes missing, Kratos and Deimos vow to find him and embark on an adventure that will put their training and Spartan spirit to the test."
God of War 20th Anniversary DualSense PS5 Controller
God of War Sons of Sparta was unable to generate the same level of hype the series' more recent entries have been known for. Despite the surprise of getting a new God of War game without any of the build-up, the prequel side-scroller generally received middling reviews from critics and fans. IGN gave it a 6/10, calling it "a pretty mediocre Metroidvania" that failed "to meet the high bar set by the titans of the genre."
Franchise creator David Jaffe was less than impressed with God of War Sons of Sparta when it launched. In a video posted at the time, he said a 2.5D God of War game is "the kind of game I've always wanted" but ultimately said it was an experience he did not like and did not recommend. He even went as far as to say, "This is not God of War."
"I wanted to make a video more about what are they thinking, like what the f*** were they thinking?" Jaffe explained. "It's not a bad game by any means, it's fine, it controls decently... but to me the more fascinating part of this is, why is this in existence? I don't understand."
What Do You Think of God of War Laufey?

item.title: Shortly after former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid a scandal involving multiple affairs and international espionage allegations, some employees of the company rallied to demand his reinstatement.
item.description:
Shortly after former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid a scandal involving multiple affairs and international espionage allegations, some employees of the company rallied to demand his reinstatement.
Nvidia's Board of Directors and the FBI launched an investigation into the 63 year old after he admitting having an affair with a woman alleged to have been a Chinese spy. The New York Times then reported that Huang had a second affair with an executive at his own company. It has since been reported that Huang had an affair with yet another Nvidia employee.
Nvidia provides advanced computer chips for everything from video games to cloud servers, but in recent years it has focused on the AI industry. Off the back of the enormous demand for memory to power data centers, Nvidia has become the world’s second-most valuable company, worth more than $4 trillion. However, stocks in the company fell on the news. Meanwhile, U.S. lawmakers on Capitol Hill have said Huang has indicated he is willing to appear before Congress for questioning.
Nvidia GeForce RTX 30-Series Reveal
In the hours after Huang's dramatic exit, a 'suggestion box' post on Nvidia's internal message board urging the company's Board of Directors to retain the CEO took off, getting around 1,600 comments, according to Wired. A majority of those comments were in support of reinstating Huang, and largely expressed sentiments that the Nvidia co-founder was instrumental to Nvidia's success over the last 33 years.
The comments themselves ranged from one employee saying, "If you believe in the mission, bring back THE boss," to, "We are all humans and can make mistakes. Jensen did so many good things and he needs a second chance."
Nvidia employees have also taken to social media to voice support for Huang. Gavan Woolery, a senior research scientist at Nvidia, posted on X / Twitter: "Jensen Huang rescued me from probably living in debt the rest of my life. I was told I was one of just three hires that he approved during the pandemic, during a hiring freeze." Woolery added: "His personal life is frankly none of my business. But as a leader, I have yet to meet a better one. Ousting him is financial suicide, and I can only assume there is a hidden ulterior motive because I can't fathom any other reason for destroying the company's value."
Bryan Cantanzaro, VP of Applied Deep Learning Research and one of the people who helped invent DLSS, took to social media to say: "I'm terribly sad @JensenHuang is no longer leading @nvidia. Thank you Jensen. For the tireless work, for the focus, for the wisdom, for the support, for the vision, for the chance you gave me to do my life's work @nvidia."
Nvidia's employees are clearly fiercely loyal to the exiting CEO. According to a Blind survey of Nvidia employees conducted by Investing.com, 88% of workers thought Huang should have stayed on. That's contrasted with a seperate poll among a wider base of professionals outside of Nvidia, where support for Huang sat at just 60%.
It's not just employees that support Huang, though. Elon Musk has spoken out in support of him, as has Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, who tweeted yesterday: "A sad day for Nvidia, developers, America, and all humanity. Jensen founded and ran one of the few companies to reach a massive scale while driving massive continued innovation and ubiquity, while others fell into the trap of ever-increasing extraction."
However, due to the amount of heat that Jensen Huang's various affairs have brought down on Nvidia, it's unlikely that he will be reinstated. Instead, Nvidia's board has appointed CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO until a permanent successor has been found. Regardless, none of this bodes well for the gaming hardware that Nvidia's current AI empire was built on top of.
Photo by Joel Saget / AFP via Getty Images.

item.title: In yet further evidence of the lengths Rockstar has gone to in order to pack GTA 6 to the brim with content, we have our first look at an animated TV series you can watch in-game.
item.description:
In yet further evidence of the lengths Rockstar has gone to in order to pack GTA 6 to the brim with content, we have our first look at an animated TV series you can watch in-game.
The DiscussingFilm X / Twitter account posted a teaser for Macca & Friends, a cartoon Rockstar created for GTA 6’s Weazel television network, which is also found in both the 3D Universe and HD Universe of the Grand Theft Auto series.
Exclusive first look at ‘MACCA & FRIENDS’.The series follows the adventures of Macca the Gator and his wetland friends across the state of Leonida. Coming November 19 on WEAZEL. https://t.co/yLpn1i3ihX
Macca & Friends has big Adult Swim vibes. It stars Pinche, a crab landlord who is going to kick out Macca the alligator if he doesn’t pay rent. There’s a talking sun, lots of other talking animals, and a police station. “The series follows the adventures of Macca the Gator and his wetland friends across the state of Leonida,” reads the description.
Reaction is a mix of disbelief that GTA 6 has an entire cartoon in the game itself to watch, and growing hype ahead of its November 19 release date. Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson recently told The New York Times that it took him about 80 hours to finish the game back in February. He noted that playthrough included the main story and some "optional goals with narrative ramifications," so it's unclear if he sat down to watch some in-game telly. Still, that is a sizable length regardless. For comparison, GTA 4 and 5 are around 30 hours long, while Red Dead Redemption 2 is around 50-60 hours. So, that means GTA 6 will be the longest of Rockstar's games to date.
GTA 6 Launch Screenshots
Indeed, an in-game TV series is exactly the kind of thing fans have come to expect from Rockstar, which operates on another level to most, if not all triple-A video game companies. We know GTA 6 did not cost more than $1.5 billion to make, but it is considered to be the most expensive video game of all time.
Rockstar has insisted GTA 6 did not cost more than $1.5 billion to make, countering an online rumor, but it’s still probably the most expensive video game of all time. A recent Bloomberg report confirmed that Rockstar Games now has 4,711 staff across 12 offices, up from the 2,441 staff it had when Red Dead Redemption 2 came out in 2018. The company has doubled in size over the last eight years, which will have increased costs significantly. But it also means Rockstar is able to do things like this cartoon, which for many fans won’t be of interest, but for some will be a fun distraction.
Bloomberg reporter Jason Schreier said in a video accompaniment to his making of GTA 6 article that Rockstar told him of a scripted system in the game that makes dual protagonists Jason and Lucia — or, it sounds like, any character in the game — exert different amounts of sweat depending on how much effort they’re putting into whatever activity they’re doing. Indeed, Rockstar set up a new studio in Los Angeles packed with writers, producers, and directors, just to make NPCs.
GTA 6 launches on November 19, and we’ve got the global release times so you know when you can start playing. This week, IGN interviewed Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick to talk GTA 6 expectations, Online, and what the next decade looks like. We’ve also got a report on the hunt for information dataminers are currently on following the launch of GTA 6 preload.

item.title: The Zelda series was in “dire straits” before Breath of the Wild, with a dwindling playerbase and low sales, according to former Nintendo marketing leads.
item.description:
The Zelda series was in “dire straits” before Breath of the Wild, with a dwindling playerbase and low sales, according to former Nintendo marketing leads.
Kit Ellis and Krysta Yang, who both worked at Nintendo for over a decade, made the claims on the latest episode of their podcast (as spotted by GamesRadar+). They refuted the idea that Breath of the Wild ruined the Zelda series with its new formula, and instead argued that it actually saved the franchise from a loss of relevance.
It comes as part of a discussion about “new Zelda” versus “old Zelda” — or essentially, the dungeon format versus a complete open world. While there is clearly a demand for the older Zelda games, as evidenced by the hugely successful Ocarina of Time remake, the pair say there is a good reason why Nintendo took them away from us in the first place.
The 10 Best Legend of Zelda Games
“There has been some revisionist history out there lately, about how the Zelda team ripped these away from us at the peak of their popularity,” Ellis says. Yang then expresses her disbelief that fans think this way. “That’s ridiculous. This series was in dire straits. They were selling, like, nothing.” Ellis goes into more detail: “I remember, I was going to the focus groups, and it was a really dark moment when the feedback [was that] the fanbase is dwindling, this is not bringing in new players.” Yang agrees again, saying that it was “depressing,” and that the playerbase was shrinking “smaller and smaller” with each new Zelda release.
Before Breath of the Wild came out in 2017, the Zelda series had seen Wii entry Skyward Sword in 2011, A Link Between Worlds in 2013, and various HD and 3D re-releases. Certainly, Breath of the Wild was an enormous hit, selling an incredible 34.28 million copes on the Switch. Its sequel, Tears of the Kingdom, came out in 2023 and has sold 22.90 million so far.
The Ocarina of Time remake looks like it continues the positive sales trend, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game so far. The question now is, what will Nintendo do with its inevitable next mainline Zelda game?
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake is out now exclusively on the Nintendo Switch 2. You can read our review of the game here, or check out our look at the Biggest Changes from the original 1998 game. Be sure to check out our expanding Ocarina of Time Remake Walkthrough for comprehensive guides on each main quest area and dungeon, plus where to get Early Heart Pieces, Early Gold Skulltulas, and Early Item Bag Expansions. If you’re looking for more, don’t miss our complete guides to All Pieces of Heart, All Gold Skulltulas, and All Empty Bottles!
Should the next Zelda return to the more traditional format?

item.title: Jason Vorhees is set to return in a 13th(!) Friday the 13th movie, the first in the horror slasher franchise in nearly 20 years.
item.description:
Jason Vorhees is set to return in a 13th(!) Friday the 13th movie, the first in the horror slasher franchise in nearly 20 years.
Word comes from Deadline, which reports Steve Miner is in place to direct the new movie due out in 2027. Miner directed 1981’s Friday the 13th Part 2, 1982’s Friday the 13th Part III, and 1998’s Halloween H20: 20 Years Later. David Fliegel is writing the script.
The last Friday the 13th movie was the 2009 reboot. New prequel series, Crystal Lake, came out on Peacock in October and finally introduced a key mission component of Jason Voorhees’ history. It became Peacock’s fourth-best scripted-original debut. IGN’s Crystal Lake review returned an 8/10. We said: “Crystal Lake works in large part thanks to Linda Cardellini’s turn as Pamela Voorhees, while showrunner Brad Caleb Kane brings a thorough knowledge of the original source material to the series.”
How to Watch the Friday the 13th Movies in Chronological Order
Deadline said the new film will be financed and produced by the Barsamian family, which controls the franchise through their company Horror, Inc. Horror, Inc. launched the ‘Jason Universe’ as part of a plan to revive the franchise in 2024.
Long-running horror franchises are on something of a tear, in movies, TV shows, and video games. For example, Illfonic's Halloween: The Game came out in September. Saber's Clive Barker's Hellraiser: Revival came out in October. Mike Flanagan adapted Stephen King's horror classic, Carrie, for a Prime Video series that's getting a Season 2. Apparently Paramount is interested in reviving A Nightmare on Elm Street, too.
